Legal

Terms of Service

Last updated November 14, 2026

The short version. Rempo is a service for businesses. We run your Google review requests and replies from the software you already use. We control the process (who gets asked, how, and when), never the results: we don't promise review counts, ratings, or rankings, and we never remove reviews. You keep ownership of your data and your accounts. You make sure you're allowed to contact your customers, and we send every message the honest way. Disputes go to individual arbitration in San Diego County, California. Please read the full terms below; they control.

1. Who we are and what these Terms cover#

These Terms of Service ("Terms") are an agreement between you and Rempo ("Rempo," "we," "us," or "our"), based in San Diego, California. They cover:

  • our websites, including rempo.io and every page under it, such as our ad landing pages (the "Site");
  • our free tools, including the Review Race, the Review Engine Scorecard, and introductory calls (the "Free Tools"); and
  • our paid services, including review requests and reminders, review replies, review monitoring and alerts, reports, review widgets, social posts made from reviews, Google Business Profile work, websites, AI receptionist features, and any software we make available with them (the "Services").

Business use only. The Site, the Free Tools, and the Services are for businesses and professionals, not for personal, family, or household use. You must be at least 18. If you use them for a company or other organization, you confirm that you have the authority to bind it, and "you" means that organization.

Other documents that are part of these Terms. These policies are incorporated into these Terms: the Acceptable Use and Review Integrity Policy, the SMS and Messaging Terms, the Billing, Renewal, and Cancellation Policy, and, when we process personal information for you, the Data Processing Addendum. If you are a HIPAA covered entity, the Business Associate Agreement also applies once you accept it. Our Privacy Policy explains how we handle personal information about you as a visitor, prospect, or client contact.

Order of precedence. If documents conflict, this order controls: (1) your Order (the checkout page, order form, or written quote you accept); (2) the Business Associate Agreement, for protected health information; (3) the Data Processing Addendum, for personal information we process for you; (4) these Terms; (5) the other policies listed above.

2. Key terms#

  • "Client" means a business that buys Services from us.
  • "Order" means the checkout page, order form, or written quote that states the Services, plan, locations, and fees you accept, including any guarantee stated there.
  • "End Customers" means your customers, patients, or clients, the people your business serves.
  • "Customer Data" means information about End Customers and your staff that you or your systems give us, or that we collect for you while providing the Services, such as names, phone numbers, email addresses, and job, visit, or case completion details.
  • "Client Content" means content you give us or approve for use, such as photos, logos, business details, message wording, and reply guidelines.
  • "Connected Accounts" means accounts we access for you, such as your Google Business Profile, your job, practice, or case management software, your social media accounts, and your website.
  • "Third-Party Platforms" means services we don't control that the Services depend on, such as Google, phone carriers, email providers, social networks, your software vendors, and the platforms we build on.
  • "AI Features" means features that use artificial intelligence to draft, summarize, or respond, such as reply drafts, social posts, and AI receptionist calls.

3. The Free Tools#

What they are. The Review Race and the Scorecard compare your public Google reviews and presence with nearby businesses, using public information at a point in time. The Review Race also shows notes and reply drafts that AI writes from public reviews; read and edit a draft before you post it, because what you post is yours. Search results change with location, device, time, and Google's own systems, so a race or report reflects what we saw when we checked.

What they are not. The Free Tools are general business information. They are not legal, financial, or professional advice, and they are not a promise of any result. We work to make them accurate but don't guarantee that they are complete, current, or error free.

No obligation. The Free Tools are free and don't require a purchase. We may change, limit, or stop offering them at any time.

Contact after you ask. When you ask for your race, a report, or a call, you ask us to send it and to contact you in the ways you chose on the form. How we use what you send is described in our Privacy Policy. Texts are covered by our SMS and Messaging Terms.

4. Accounts and access you give us#

Your account details. Give us accurate business and contact information and keep it current. Keep any login we give you secure. You are responsible for what happens under your logins and for the people you give access to. Tell us right away at support@rempo.io if you suspect unauthorized access.

Access to your Connected Accounts. To run the Services we need access to some of your accounts, for example a manager invitation to your Google Business Profile and a connection to the software where you record completed jobs. When you give us that access:

  • you authorize us, our staff, and our service providers to access and act in those accounts as needed to provide the Services you bought, and for nothing else;
  • you confirm that you own or control those accounts, or have the owner's permission, and that giving us access doesn't break the account's own terms;
  • you keep ownership of your accounts, and you can remove our access at any time (Services that depend on that access will stop, and fees continue until you cancel); and
  • we prefer invitations and connections over shared passwords. If you choose to share a password, we use it only for the Services and protect it as confidential.

When the Services end, we remove our own access where we can, and you should confirm that our manager roles, connections, and API keys are removed from your accounts.

5. The Services#

What we provide. We provide the Services described in your Order and in the plan details shown when you bought. Depending on your plan, this may include: review requests sent to End Customers after completed work recorded in your connected system, one reminder, replies written for your reviews, alerts when a review posts, a monthly report, a review widget for your website, social posts made from your reviews, Google Business Profile work, website design and hosting, and AI receptionist features.

What you do. The Services depend on a few things from you. You agree to:

  • connect the system where you record completed work, and keep that connection working;
  • give us access to your Google Business Profile and any other Connected Accounts your plan needs;
  • send the photo, logo, and business details we ask for;
  • review and approve your message wording, reply guidelines, and texting registration details before launch, and answer our approval requests in a reasonable time;
  • give us accurate Customer Data and tell us promptly about any End Customer who asked you not to contact them; and
  • follow these Terms, the Acceptable Use and Review Integrity Policy, and the laws that apply to your business.

Approvals. Before we send anything for you, you approve your request messages and reply guidelines. Replies to negative reviews are sent for your approval unless you tell us in writing to post them directly. Messages and replies we send for you are your business's statements, sent in your name, and you are responsible for content you approve or tell us to use.

Timelines. Dates and timelines we give are estimates, unless your Order states a guarantee. They move when we are waiting on you (access, approvals, data) or on a Third-Party Platform (for example, carrier texting registration or a Google review of your profile).

Text messaging registration. Business texting in the United States requires registration with the carriers (often called A2P 10DLC), using your business's details. The carriers decide whether and when to approve it. We can't guarantee approval or timing. Email requests can often start before texting is approved.

Third-Party Platforms. The Services run on platforms we don't control. Google, carriers, and other providers may change their features, rules, or prices; filter, delay, or block messages; remove or hide reviews; or restrict or suspend your accounts. That is not a breach of these Terms by us. When it happens, we will tell you what we know and make reasonable efforts to adapt the Services.

Changes to the Services. We may update and improve the Services. If a change materially reduces the core Services you are paying for during a paid period, we will tell you in advance, and you may cancel and receive a refund of fees you prepaid for the period after the change.

Our team and providers. We may use employees, contractors, and service providers to deliver the Services, in the United States or elsewhere. We remain responsible for their work under these Terms. Our current providers are listed on our Subprocessors page.

6. No guaranteed results#

We control the process: asking every eligible End Customer the same way, following up once, writing replies, and reporting what happened. We don't control what people do or what Google and other platforms do. So:

  • We don't guarantee any number of reviews, any star rating, any search ranking or position, any number of calls, leads, or sales, or any revenue.
  • We don't guarantee that any platform will publish, keep, or display a particular review, or that it won't restrict your profile.
  • We don't remove reviews, write reviews, buy reviews, or screen out unhappy customers.

If your Order includes a guarantee, it covers only what it states (for example, a go-live date or replies within a set time), under the conditions stated there and in our Billing, Renewal, and Cancellation Policy. A guarantee's stated remedy is your only remedy for missing it.

7. Compliance: who is responsible for what#

Rempo sends messages and posts replies as your service provider, on your behalf and in your business's name. The rules on contacting people and on reviews apply to you as the business, and to us as the one sending. Here is how we share that work.

You are responsible for:

  • having the consent or other legal basis the law requires to contact each End Customer by text, email, or phone, including under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, the CAN-SPAM Act, state telemarketing and texting laws, and carrier rules. Our SMS and Messaging Terms include model consent wording for your forms;
  • honoring opt-outs you receive directly, and telling us about them;
  • the accuracy of Customer Data and the content you approve;
  • the professional rules that apply to your business, such as HIPAA and state medical privacy laws, state bar rules, financial adviser marketing rules, and licensing board rules; and
  • following review platform policies and the FTC's rules on reviews and endorsements in everything you do outside the Services.

We are responsible for:

  • sending the same request to every eligible End Customer, with no screening by sentiment, no incentives, and no suggested wording;
  • including clear opt-out instructions and honoring opt-outs we receive (reply STOP to texts, unsubscribe links in emails) across your messages;
  • scheduling texts for daytime hours, between 9 a.m. and 8 p.m. in your business's local time zone, unless you give us a narrower window;
  • using Customer Data only to provide the Services, as described in the Data Processing Addendum; and
  • protecting Customer Data with reasonable security measures.

Our right to refuse. We may decline to send a message, post a reply, or run a campaign that we reasonably believe would break the law, a platform's rules, or our Acceptable Use and Review Integrity Policy. We may suspend sending while we look into a complaint, a carrier notice, or a compliance concern.

8. Healthcare practices, law firms, and advisers#

Healthcare. If you are a HIPAA covered entity, don't send us protected health information until our Business Associate Agreement is in place. Tell us if you are a covered entity. Our replies never confirm that a reviewer is a patient and never mention care. Before we use a patient's review in a social post or on your website, you must have the patient's written authorization where HIPAA or state law requires it. We don't accept records protected by 42 C.F.R. Part 2 (substance use disorder treatment records). Veterinary practices are generally outside HIPAA, but state privacy rules may still apply.

Law firms. Only send us a client's contact details if that client has agreed to be contacted for a review, for example through a consent line in your engagement or closing letter. Replies we write reveal no client information. Nothing of value is offered for a review. You remain responsible for your professional obligations under your state's rules of professional conduct.

Financial advisers. If the SEC Marketing Rule or similar rules apply to you, you are responsible for the disclosures they require when you use testimonials or reviews in marketing.

We are not your lawyers. Rempo doesn't give legal advice. Our templates and practices are built around common rules, but you should confirm with your own advisers what applies to your business.

9. AI Features#

How we use AI. Some Services use AI tools, including tools from third-party providers, to draft replies, write social posts, summarize reviews, and, if you buy it, answer calls. AI output can be wrong or incomplete. Depending on your plan, a person on our team reviews AI drafts, and you approve the guidelines they follow.

Your data and AI training. We don't use Customer Data to train AI models, and we choose AI providers whose business terms don't allow them to use your data to train their general models.

AI receptionist. If you use an AI receptionist:

  • callers must be told they are speaking with an automated assistant wherever the law requires it, and the assistant must never claim to be a person or a licensed professional;
  • calls are recorded only with the notices and consent the law requires (California and several other states require the consent of everyone on the call), and you must keep those notices in place; and
  • we won't place outbound AI-voice calls or send prerecorded messages unless you show us the prior express consent the law requires for each person called.

10. Content, data, and ownership#

Your data and content are yours. You own Customer Data and Client Content. You give us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to host, copy, use, adapt, and display them only to provide and support the Services, to keep them secure, and to comply with the law. That includes placing your photo, logo, and business name in your review requests, images, replies, and posts.

Reviews belong to the people who write them. Reviews on Google and other platforms are written by reviewers and governed by those platforms' terms. When we show or quote reviews for you (on a widget or in a social post), we use the reviewer's first name or initials and don't change the meaning. You are responsible for making sure your use of reviews follows the platform's terms and, for healthcare, the patient authorization rules in Section 8.

Aggregated statistics. We may create aggregated, de-identified statistics from use of the Services (for example, average request response rates across clients) to run and improve the Services. They never identify you, your End Customers, or any person. Protected health information is used only as the Business Associate Agreement allows.

Feedback. If you send us suggestions, we may use them without any obligation to you.

Our property. We and our licensors own the Site, the Free Tools, our software, templates, report formats, workflows, and know-how, and everything we create that isn't a Custom Deliverable. Subject to these Terms and payment, you may use the deliverables we provide in your business while you are a Client. You may not copy, resell, or reverse engineer our software or templates.

Websites we build. When you have paid in full for a website build, you own the website design and content we created specifically for you (the "Custom Deliverables"). Our pre-existing tools, templates, code, and third-party components (such as themes, plugins, fonts, and stock images, each under its own license) stay ours or their owners', and we grant you a license to use them as part of your website. If we host your website and the hosting ends, we will give you an export of the website files and content on request made within 30 days.

Your data when the Services end. For 30 days after the Services end, you may ask us for an export of your Customer Data that we still hold. After that, we delete it as described in the Data Processing Addendum.

11. Fees, payment, and renewal#

Fees. You agree to pay the fees in your Order, which may include a recurring fee for each location or Google profile, one-time setup fees, and add-ons. The full price, how often you are charged, and any setup fee are shown before you pay.

Recurring billing. Paid plans renew automatically at the end of each billing period (monthly or annual, as stated in your Order) until you cancel. By subscribing, you authorize us and our payment processor to charge your payment method for each renewal period and any other fees you agree to. For annual plans, we email you a reminder between 15 and 45 days before each renewal.

Commitments and waived fees. If your Order waives a fee in exchange for a commitment (for example, a waived setup fee for a 12-month commitment) and you end the Services before the commitment period ends, the waived amount becomes due, as stated in your Order.

Price changes. We may change prices for future billing periods. We will email you at least 30 days before a price increase takes effect, and you may cancel before then. A price we promised to hold for you (such as a founding price) stays as promised.

Taxes. Fees don't include taxes. You pay any sales, use, value-added, or similar taxes on the Services, other than taxes on our income.

Late or failed payments. If a payment fails, we will notify you and retry. If it remains unpaid 10 days after our notice, we may suspend the Services until it is paid. Overdue amounts may accrue interest at 1% per month or the highest rate the law allows, whichever is lower.

Billing questions. If you think a charge is wrong, contact us at support@rempo.io within 60 days. We will work with you in good faith. Please contact us before disputing a charge with your bank.

Details on renewals, cancellation, refunds, and guarantees are in our Billing, Renewal, and Cancellation Policy.

12. Cancellation and refunds#

You can cancel at any time, online in your billing portal when we have given you one, or by emailing support@rempo.io. Cancellation takes effect at the end of your current billing period; you keep the Services until then and won't be charged again. We may offer you one alternative (for example, a smaller plan) when you cancel. You can decline it and cancel in the same step.

Refunds. Fees are not refunded for partial billing periods, and setup fees are not refunded once setup work has started, except: (a) as a guarantee in your Order provides; (b) if we end the Services for our convenience, or a change materially reduces the Services as described in Section 5, in which case we refund prepaid fees for the unused period; or (c) where the law requires a refund.

13. Term, suspension, and termination#

Term. These Terms apply from your first use of the Site or the Free Tools. A paid subscription runs from purchase until it is cancelled or terminated.

Suspension. We may suspend all or part of the Services, with notice where practical, if: payment is overdue as described in Section 11; you or your users break the Acceptable Use and Review Integrity Policy; a carrier, Google, or another platform requires it; there is a security risk; or the law requires it. We will restore the Services once the cause is resolved.

Termination. Either of us may terminate the Services if the other materially breaches these Terms and doesn't fix the breach within 15 days after written notice. We may terminate immediately if you seriously or repeatedly break the Acceptable Use and Review Integrity Policy, or if continuing would expose us to legal liability. We may also end the Services for our convenience on 30 days' notice, with a refund of prepaid fees for the unused period.

What happens at the end. Your access ends and we stop sending messages for you. Fees owed up to the end date remain due. You can ask for your data as described in Section 10. Sections that by their nature should survive (including Sections 6, 10, 14, and 16 through 20) survive.

14. Confidentiality#

Each of us may receive the other's non-public business information ("Confidential Information"). The receiving party will use it only to perform under these Terms, protect it with at least reasonable care, and share it only with people and providers who need it for that purpose and are bound to protect it. Confidential Information doesn't include information that is public through no fault of the receiving party, was already known to it, was independently developed, or was rightfully received from someone else without a duty of confidence. A party may disclose Confidential Information when the law requires, after giving the other party notice where the law allows. These duties last for three years after the Services end, and for trade secrets and Customer Data, for as long as the information stays protected.

15. Privacy and security#

Our Privacy Policy explains how we handle personal information about visitors, prospects, and client contacts. When we process Customer Data for you, we act as your service provider under the Data Processing Addendum, which includes the terms California law requires for service providers. Protected health information is handled under the Business Associate Agreement. We maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards appropriate to the nature of the information, and we notify you of security incidents as the Data Processing Addendum describes.

Each of us promises that it has the authority to enter into these Terms and will comply with the laws that apply to it in performing them.

We promise to perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards. If we don't, tell us within 30 days of the problem. We will re-perform the affected Services, and if we can't, we will refund the fees you paid for the affected Services for the affected period. That is your remedy for a breach of this promise.

You promise that you have the rights, consents, and permissions needed for the Customer Data, Client Content, and Connected Accounts you give us, and that our use of them as these Terms allow won't violate the law or anyone's rights.

17. Indemnification#

By you. You will defend us, our owners, staff, and contractors against any third-party claim, investigation, or demand, and pay the resulting losses, damages, fines, settlements, and reasonable attorneys' fees, to the extent it arises from: (a) Customer Data or Client Content, including any claim that you lacked consent to contact an End Customer; (b) messages, replies, or other content sent at your instruction or with your approval; (c) your violation of the law, these Terms, the Acceptable Use and Review Integrity Policy, or a platform's rules; (d) your products and services, and your dealings with End Customers, employees, and reviewers; or (e) your professional obligations, such as your duties as a HIPAA covered entity or under bar rules.

By us. We will defend you against any third-party claim, and pay the resulting losses, damages, settlements, and reasonable attorneys' fees, to the extent it arises from: (a) a claim that our software or materials, as we provide them, infringe a United States patent, copyright, or trademark, or misappropriate a trade secret (this doesn't cover Client Content, Third-Party Platforms, AI output you change or direct, or combinations we didn't make); or (b) our willful misconduct or knowing violation of the law in providing the Services. If an infringement claim is made or likely, we may get you the right to keep using the item, change it so it doesn't infringe, or end the affected Services and refund prepaid fees for the unused period.

How it works. The party seeking defense must notify the other promptly, let it control the defense and settlement, and cooperate reasonably, at the defending party's expense. A delay in notice reduces the defending party's duty only to the extent the delay harms it. No settlement may admit fault for, or impose an obligation on, the defended party without its consent, which won't be unreasonably withheld.

No indirect damages. TO THE FULLEST EXTENT THE LAW ALLOWS, NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, REVENUE, BUSINESS, GOODWILL, OR DATA, EVEN IF ADVISED THEY WERE POSSIBLE.

TO THE FULLEST EXTENT THE LAW ALLOWS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THESE TERMS AND THE SERVICES WILL NOT EXCEED THE FEES YOU PAID US IN THE 12 MONTHS BEFORE THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE LIABILITY. 19. Disputes and arbitration#

Talk to us first. Before starting a formal claim, the party with the dispute will send a written notice describing it to the other (to us at legal@rempo.io), and we will both try in good faith to resolve it within 30 days.

Binding individual arbitration. If we can't resolve it, any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or relating to these Terms, the Site, the Free Tools, or the Services, including whether this section applies, will be resolved by final and binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (AAA) under its Commercial Arbitration Rules then in effect, before a single arbitrator. The arbitration will be seated in San Diego County, California, and may be held by video conference. The Federal Arbitration Act governs this section. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court with jurisdiction.

No class or representative actions. Claims may be brought only on an individual basis, not as a plaintiff or class member in any class, collective, consolidated, or representative action. The arbitrator may not combine claims of different parties. If this paragraph is found unenforceable for a particular claim, that claim must be decided in court as described below, and the arbitration provisions won't apply to it.

Exceptions. Either party may bring an individual claim in small claims court, and either party may ask a court for an injunction or other equitable relief to stop the misuse of its intellectual property or Confidential Information.

Costs. Fees for the arbitration are paid as the AAA rules provide. Each party pays its own attorneys' fees, unless the arbitrator awards fees as the law or these Terms allow.

Time limit. To the extent the law allows, a claim must be started within one year after it arises, or it is permanently barred.

20. Governing law and venue#

California law governs these Terms, without regard to conflict of laws rules, except that the Federal Arbitration Act governs Section 19. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply. For any matter that is not arbitrated, the state and federal courts located in San Diego County, California, have exclusive jurisdiction, and both parties consent to them.

If a change is material, we will also email Clients at least 30 days before it takes effect, unless the change is required sooner by law. Continued use after a change takes effect means you accept it. If you don't agree, cancel before the change takes effect. Changes don't apply to disputes that arose before the change was posted.

  • Compliance with trade laws. You may not use the Services in violation of United States export control or sanctions laws.
